masonry.value: Plano historically required high masonry percentages on single-family exteriors; after HB 2439 (2019, Gov't Code ch. 3000) cities may not require materials beyond national model codes except in exempt cases (e.g. historic districts). Plano's current enforcement and any PD/historic exceptions not verified. HOA/deed restrictions in Plano subdivisions very commonly require masonry.

plainLanguage: Plano's rules could not be checked online during this research, so the numbers here are provisional. The common SF-7 zone is for lots of about 7,000 sq ft, with front yards believed to be 25 ft and side yards 5 ft. Check your plat and HOA rules, which are often stricter. A 2019 state law stops the city from requiring brick or stone, but many Plano HOAs still require it. Plan on an engineer-designed foundation because of the clay soils. Plano is in energy climate zone 3A.
